findings.title: 10 of 15 suburban wards but 2 of 9 island-city wards are in the two highest incident classes - and ward population alone ranks wards with Spearman rho = 0.83
findings.method: Ordinal incident class per ward digitised from BMC FPG 2026 p.18 (colour-matched to legend, 3 sample points per ward, 24/24 unanimous); population from Census 2011 aggregated to wards.
caveats: Counts are complaint/incident records (source: 'CCS'), so they reflect reporting as well as flooding.
Only the class bin is known, not the exact count.

findings.title: Three official lists name 251 distinct places, but only 16 (6%) appear on more than one list
findings.method: Same-ward matching: fuzzy name tokens (Jaccard >= 0.5, >= 2 shared tokens) or geocodes within 250 m plus partial name match; never merging two records of one source. Edition similarity = word-level SequenceMatcher ratio of BEST Annex IX text.
findings.period: BMC FPG 2026 (incl. Mumbai Traffic Police table); BEST booklets 2023-24, 2024-25, 2026
findings.sample: 97 BMC rows (24 wards), 84 BEST rows (9 island-city wards), 90 traffic-police rows (19 ward headings)
caveats: The lists serve different purposes (BMC: dewatering pumps; BEST: switching off electricity; traffic police: diversions), so they need not match - but none can be treated as complete.
Name matching can miss the same place written very differently, so overlap may be understated.

findings.title: Monsoon rain is extremely concentrated, and global-model rainfall misses Mumbai's extremes
findings.method: IMD monthly grid 19.00N 72.75E (1901-2021); ERA5 daily via Open-Meteo (1991-2025); Theil-Sen slope + Kendall tau for trends; heavy day = IMD category >= 64.5 mm/24 h.
caveats: ERA5 is a ~25 km model estimate; both Mumbai reference points fall in one cell, so it cannot show rainfall differences between neighbourhoods.
The 944 mm figure is a station record quoted by BMC; ERA5 is an area average, so some gap is expected - the size of the gap is the point.

findings.title: Terrain (90 m DEM) does not clearly separate listed spots from the rest of their ward
findings.method: Copernicus GLO-90 DEM via Open-Meteo; TPI = elevation minus median of 500 m grid cells within 1 km; each location's percentile among its own ward's grid cells; Wilcoxon signed-rank vs 0.5.
caveats: GLO-90 is a 90 m surface model including buildings; vertical error is metres.
Geocoding error (tens to hundreds of metres) blurs the comparison.
Listed spots are not a random sample of flooded places.

findings.title: 43 of 97 BMC-listed spots have no dewatering pump recorded against them
findings.method: Direct counts from the transcribed BMC FPG 2026 ward directory.
caveats: A blank pump cell may mean no pump, a pump recorded elsewhere, or a mitigated spot - the source does not say.
Capacity figures are incomplete for several multi-pump spots.

findings.title: After a heavy-rain day, the next day is heavy 43% of the time, against 6% after other monsoon days
findings.method: Heavy-rain day = IMD 0.25 deg gridded rain >= 64.5 mm in either Mumbai cell. Conditional shares over June-September days, 1971-2016; outlook model tested on later years only (predict.py).
caveats: A 25 km cell average under-states point extremes (26 July 2005, Santacruz).
Heavy rain is the trigger, not the outcome: waterlogging also depends on drains, tide and pumps.
City-wide only: it cannot say which neighbourhood will flood.

imd.source: IMD gridded monthly rainfall, grid point 19.00N 72.75E, via OpenCity

era5.source: ERA5 reanalysis daily precipitation via Open-Meteo Historical Weather API
era5.2005_07_26_reference_source: BMC Flood Preparedness Guidelines 2026, p.17 (Santacruz record)

sensitivity.tier_rule: A = top 20% of ranks, B = next 30%, C = remaining 50% (relative order, not risk level)

pump_gap.title: No pump recorded
pump_gap.rule: On BMC's 2026 list of waterlogging spots, with the dewatering-pump cell blank
pump_gap.check: Confirm whether a pump is assigned, moved or no longer needed; record it before the monsoon

list_gap.title: Missing from BMC's list
list_gap.rule: Named by BEST or the Traffic Police, but not by BMC's own 2026 list
list_gap.check: Ask the ward office to confirm the spot and add it to the BMC list, or record why not

corroborated.title: Named by 2+ lists
corroborated.rule: Independent official lists agree on this place
corroborated.check: Pre-monsoon drain, culvert and outfall check

traffic_critical.title: Traffic diversion planned
traffic_critical.rule: Mumbai Traffic Police divert traffic here when it waterlogs
traffic_critical.check: Agree the alert contact with the traffic division before heavy-rain days

needs_location.title: Exact spot unknown
needs_location.rule: The official name could only be placed at neighbourhood level, or not at all
needs_location.check: Field-verify the exact spot and record its coordinates

allocation.rule: Walk down the priority order and take each place unless its ward already has 3; stop at 20.

observed_model.target: Tomorrow is a heavy-rain day: IMD gridded rain >= 64.5 mm in either Mumbai cell
observed_model.timing: Issued at 08:30 IST from the 24 h just measured; predicts the next 24 h (IMD rain day)

forecast_track_record.source: Open-Meteo Previous Runs API, precipitation_previous_day1, Santacruz point (19.0896 N, 72.8656 E)
forecast_track_record.caveat: Two monsoons only; one forecast point vs the wetter of two 25 km observed cells. Shares are descriptive frequencies, not a validated probability model.
